content.overview: Quality is not created by one final test. A postharvest quality system links controlled procedures, competent work, equipment, records, deviations and visible material status across the process.

vocabulary.definition: Coordinated controls used to direct and demonstrate consistent quality activities.
Controlled designation such as in process, hold, released or otherwise authorized.
Approved criterion and context used by an authorized process to evaluate evidence.

sections.title: Controls work as a system
sections.body: Procedures, training, equipment, monitoring and records should support the same process rather than existing as disconnected documents.

sections.title: Status prevents unintended use
sections.body: Physical labels, locations and electronic records should agree and changes should be attributable to an authorized role.

sections.title: Data integrity supports reconstruction
sections.body: Records should remain attributable, contemporaneous, complete and available through their lifecycle.

workedExamples: A released label on material while the electronic record says hold is a system failure requiring reconciliation before movement.
commonMistakes: Treating final testing as the entire quality system.
Keeping procedures that do not match actual work.
content.practicalApplication: Map one postharvest process step to its procedure, training, equipment check, record, deviation path and lot-status control.
content.summary: A postharvest QMS aligns how work is defined, performed, recorded, reviewed and authorized.
